chunks: He is God; there is no god but He, the knower of the unknown and the known. He is the benevolent, ever-merciful.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's knowledge of the unseen and the seen?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited as the opening of the 'Tasniyah' (the double recitation) in Surah Al-Anfal, uniquely repeats the declaration of Tawhid and divine attributes found in Surah At-Taghabun, highlighting the continuity of God's knowledge and mercy across different contexts of revelation. Shia scholars emphasize the dual aspect of His knowledge over both the hidden realities (ghayb) and the manifest world (shadah) as a foundation for understanding divine providence. The attribution of Rahman (universal mercy) and Rahim (specific mercy) underscores the balance between God's general benevolence to all creation and His special care for the believers.
